description: Schematic visual guidance retrieval; AI expectations are manual review criteria, not measured behavior.

cases.prompt: Review schematic appearance and connectivity separately
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. This checklist is not an automatic layout or correctness guarantee.

cases.prompt: Keep a consistent signal-flow convention
cases.ai_expectation: Feedback, bidirectional links and bridges need exceptions; do not change circuitry for appearance.

cases.prompt: Group related circuitry with meaningful headings
cases.ai_expectation: A small sheet can contain several groups; one sheet per block is not mandatory.

cases.prompt: Use hierarchy to make large designs navigable
cases.ai_expectation: Excessive nesting can hinder review; select depth for the design.

cases.prompt: Draw repeated channels consistently
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. Do not copy incorrect values or join independent nets to create symmetry.

cases.prompt: Reserve space for annotations and wire escape
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. There is no universal millimeter gap; enlarge or split the drawing rather than shrink everything.

cases.prompt: Use a connectivity-compatible schematic grid
cases.ai_expectation: A PCB placement grid is not a schematic connection grid.

cases.prompt: Arrange symbol pins for function, not package shape
cases.ai_expectation: KLC is a library convention, not authorization to swap electrical pins.

cases.prompt: Keep visible wire paths easy to follow
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. Diagonal bridge drawings can be clearer; schematic paths are not PCB routes.

cases.prompt: Distinguish junctions from wire crossings
cases.ai_expectation: Graphic dots are not electrical junctions.

cases.prompt: Make label scope explicit across sheets
cases.ai_expectation: Replacing label types can change connectivity.

cases.prompt: Keep bus members and names explicit
cases.ai_expectation: Visual bundling does not prove connectivity.

cases.prompt: Use short meaningful net names consistently
cases.ai_expectation: Renaming a net can alter connectivity and downstream constraints.

cases.prompt: Show active-low meaning without ambiguous notation
cases.ai_expectation: KLC pin formatting is not a requirement to rename all project nets.

cases.prompt: Align related interface pins to reduce crossings
cases.ai_expectation: Only graphical ordering is discussed; physical pin reassignment needs separate authorization and verification.

cases.prompt: Mark intentionally unused pins accurately
cases.ai_expectation: Do not suppress required connections for appearance.

cases.prompt: Keep annotations clear of wires and pin text
cases.ai_expectation: An electrical check does not establish visual readability.

cases.prompt: Check text at the intended reading scale
cases.ai_expectation: KLC values are library conventions, not a universal typography standard.

cases.prompt: Keep power and ground presentation consistent
cases.ai_expectation: Ground symbol appearance does not establish isolation or justify merging grounds.

cases.prompt: Account for every unit and its power connections
cases.ai_expectation: KLC separates shared power for multi-unit symbols; it does not recommend removing power from single-unit symbols.

cases.prompt: Keep local feedback and support circuits understandable
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. Drawing proximity does not specify physical PCB placement.

cases.prompt: State connector orientation when pin interpretation matters
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. Schematic symbol position is not a physical connector view.

cases.prompt: Show essential values, configuration and design intent
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. Do not substitute prose for electrical connections or formal assembly data.

cases.prompt: Review the final exported schematic independently
cases.ai_expectation: Editorial convention, not a source-mandated rule. A render review complements ERC; neither proves circuit operation.
